The handbook was developed to support the implementation of the Global Strategy on Human Resources for Health: Workforce 2030, which aims to ensure a health workforce that is fit for purpose to achieve universal health coverage (UHC) and the health-related targets of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The strategy emphasizes the importance of adequate investment and effective policies to strengthen health systems and ensure universal accessibility, acceptability, coverage, and quality of health workforces. The handbook outlines the challenges faced by health workforces globally, including issues in education, training, deployment, performance, and retention. Suboptimal allocation of health workers directly impacts the availability, accessibility, quality, and performance of national health services, potentially leaving populations without adequate access to necessary health services. These challenges hinder progress toward achieving UHC and the SDGs. The WHO and its partners developed the Global Strategy on Human Resources for Health to address these challenges. The strategy provides a policy agenda to ensure a health workforce that meets the needs of populations and supports the attainment of UHC and SDG targets. Achieving these goals requires sufficient investment and the implementation of effective policies at national, regional, and global levels.
